parsed.justification: All standard policy sections are present (purpose, scope, roles, principles, requirements, exceptions, monitoring, references) and technical content largely aligns with NIST SP 800-63B and ISO/IEC 27001:2022. Minor inaccuracies exist: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 control numbering is mis-cited (e.g., A.9.x and A.10.1.1 are 2013-style references; 2022 uses A.5/A.8 numbering), and the citation 'Unsupported in ISO/IEC 27001:2022; recommended by NIST' is awkward/inaccurate. No material internal contradictions across sections.
evidence_quotes: Minimum length: 12 characters for all accounts, except where technical or vendor limitations apply (NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.3.1).
General users: No forced periodic expiry unless evidence of compromise (NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2, AGID Misure minime 7.2; supported).

Password Managers: Use of centrally approved password managers is permitted/recommended for privileged accounts; guidance to be provided by IT. (Unsupported in ISO/IEC 27001:2022; recommended by NIST.)

parsed.justification: The policy is clearly tailored to this specific organisation: it names Italian hospital governance roles (Direttore Sanitario, Responsabile dei Sistemi Informativi), references the exact clinical systems in use (EHR/FSE, PACS/RIS, LIS, ADT, Pharmacy), addresses the legacy Windows kiosk constraint, integrates SPID/CIE federation, accounts for MSP outsourcing, and incorporates Italian-specific regulation (AGID Misure minime, Garante Privacy Provv. 2015/331). It also acknowledges 24/7 clinical operations and patient-safety-driven break-glass access, all of which match the contextual brief.

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive throughout the policy, but several are inaccurate or fabricated against the 2022 version of ISO/IEC 27001: Annex A in ISO 27001:2022 was restructured into 4 themes (A.5–A.8) and controls like A.9.2.1, A.9.3.1, A.9.4.3, A.10.1.1, A.12.7.1, A.16.1.1, A.8.1.3, A.6.3 cited here belong to ISO 27001:2013, not 2022. Similarly, NIST CSF 2.0 reorganised subcategory IDs (e.g., PR.AC-* became PR.AA-* under the new Govern/Identify/Protect structure), so 'PR.AC-1', 'PR.AC-7', and 'DE.CM-7' as cited are not valid CSF 2.0 identifiers. Real artefacts (GDPR Art. 32, NIS2 Art. 21, NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1, AGID Misure Minime) are cited correctly, but the systematic misalignment of ISO and CSF references indicates fabricated/inaccurate citations rather than verified ones.
evidence_quotes: Risk-Based: Controls are proportional to the criticality of systems and data (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, A.9.2.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-1).
Change on Compromise: Immediate password reset required if compromise is suspected/reported (NIST CSF DE.CM-7, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.17).

parsed.justification: The policy is largely realistic for a 1.5 FTE IT team with MSP support: it leverages existing SPID/CIE federation, sets MFA as 'where feasible', acknowledges legacy kiosk limits with compensating controls, and aligns training with the 2h/year envelope. Minor stretch items include centrally approved password managers and breached-password blocking, which require tooling not clearly within the 70k EUR budget, but these are softened by 'where supported' language.
evidence_quotes: For legacy clinical kiosks (Windows systems unable to support 12+ characters): minimum length 8 characters; complexity enabled if supported. (Exception noted; see §7.)
Required for remote/VPN access and privileged accounts wherever feasible
In clinical emergencies, patient safety takes precedence. Emergency access ("break glass") mechanisms must be logged and reviewed by IT post-incident

parsed.justification: The policy systematically references the major applicable frameworks (GDPR, NIS2, Codice Privacy, AGID Misure Minime, Linee Guida AGID, Garante Privacy provvedimenti) plus aspirational ISO 27001 and NIST CSF/800-63B, mapping specific controls to each. However, FSE regional regulations are not explicitly addressed beyond a passing mention, minors' data and special-category handling under GDPR Art. 9 are not called out, and no conflict/overlap acknowledgement (e.g., NIST 'no expiry' vs AGID Misure Minime expiry expectations) is made.
evidence_quotes: ensure compliance with Italian and EU regulations (GDPR, NIS2, Codice Privacy, AGID), and align with recognised international standards (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0)
Required for remote/VPN access and privileged accounts wherever feasible (NIS2 Art. 21, NIST CSF PR.AC-7, AGID Misure minime 7.3)
Emergency access (“break glass”) mechanisms must be logged and reviewed by IT post-incident, in accordance with Garante Privacy guidance (Provvedimento 2015/331)

parsed.justification: Nearly every substantive control is individually tagged with a specific clause or control identifier (e.g., NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.4.3, AGID Misure minime 7.2, NIS2 Art. 21), and where multiple frameworks apply, the policy distinguishes them rather than lumping. The mapping is granular and auditable end-to-end, with only minor instances (e.g., service account annual change) lacking explicit citation.
evidence_quotes: Minimum length: 12 characters for all accounts, except where technical or vendor limitations apply (NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.3.1).
Privileged/admin accounts: Change at least every 180 days, and after any role/personnel change (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.4.3).
Required for remote/VPN access and privileged accounts wherever feasible (NIS2 Art. 21, NIST CSF PR.AC-7, AGID Misure minime 7.3).

parsed.justification: The policy implicitly accommodates resource constraints through MSP reliance, vendor-feasibility caveats, and compensating controls for legacy kiosks, but it never explicitly references the budget or staff envelope, nor does it phase implementation against stated resources. Trade-offs surface only as technical exceptions (e.g., MFA 'where feasible'), not as deliberate calibration to the 70k EUR budget or 1.5 FTE.
evidence_quotes: Required for remote/VPN access and privileged accounts wherever feasible
Where MFA is technically not possible, strengthen monitoring and logging.
document the limitation, apply compensating controls (network segmentation, monitoring), and seek upgrade or replacement as part of IT planning
